The implementation is complete and the build is green (the single test class, `AcceptanceTest`, passes; the other two files are test helpers, not test classes).

## Summary

The change de-duplicates a new owner's `customerCode` against existing owners before saving.

**`OwnerCustomerCodes.java`** — added a focused `deduplicate(base, taken)` helper alongside the existing formatting methods. It returns `base` when free, otherwise the first `base-<n>` (starting at n=2) not already taken. This keeps the "customer code" rules together while staying a distinct, single-purpose method.

**`AssignOwnerCustomerCode.java`** — now injects `OwnerRepository` (the same pattern as sibling steps like `AssignOwnerNamesakeCount`), collects the non-null `customerCode`s of existing owners, and stores the de-duplicated result. Since this step runs before `save`, `findAll()` never includes the new owner itself.

The de-dup logic lives in the code-formatting class; the function class stays a thin orchestrator that reads existing state and applies the result — no class became a catch-all, and the existing `forOwner`/`format`/`hash8` code is reused unchanged.
